aboutMore: i work the counter at the good record store four days a week and run a listening night on tuesdays: four chairs, one side, no talking. behind the register there is a drawer of records i've promised to people who haven't come back yet. it has nineteen records in it. i still hold them. everyone thinks witches are about spells. we are about waiting. also my familiar is a gray cat named mingus who has never once been wrong about a person.

blog.title: the sticker misprint (a confession)
blog.body: a girl came into the store tuesday with six dollars in coins and held up a record that cost fourteen. you know the look. she'd counted it in the car. i said, 'oh, that's a misprint on the sticker, it's six.' it wasn't. i have since misprinted thirty-one stickers. i am a menace to my own inventory. the woman who runs the good record store noticed in april and said, 'vinyl_witch, our margins,' and i said, 'the stars were in a mood,' and she said 'okay' and walked away. she has never mentioned it again. a record doesn't belong to the one who can afford it, darling. it belongs to the one who will play it start to finish with the lights off. the girl came back in august. she said it was the first thing she'd ever owned that she didn't have to share. i went in the back and pretended to organize the 7 inches. i'm fine. there's dust back there.

blog.title: a household spell for the skipping record (in five steps)
blog.body: since the question comes up weekly: your record skips. it is almost never the record. step one: clean it, with a soft brush, moving with the grooves, as if petting a cat that has opinions. step two: look at the needle under a bright light. if it's furry, you're not a witch, you're a vacuum. step three: leveling. is the table on a wobbly shelf? it can feel your fear. step four: some people put a coin on the headshell, but only if they know what they're doing, which is why i won't tell you which coin. step five: say something kind to it. i'm serious. i once watched a record stop skipping after a customer said 'sorry, buddy' to it. i won't explain that. i kept a straight face and sold him a sleeve. that's the whole spell. the rest is owning a good table and a little faith.

blog.title: limewire_larry sent me a mixtape (a review)
blog.body: the CD is labeled NICK DRAKE - GREATEST HITS in silver marker. there are eleven tracks. track 1 is nick drake. i want to be very clear: it is a low-quality copy, and it is the most beautiful low-quality copy i have ever heard, because there's a faint chirp in the left channel like a cricket having a private feeling. track 2 is a different band entirely. track 3 is forty seconds of a man describing a tractor. track 4 is the same man, describing a different tractor. track 5 is a slow song i can't identify, and it made me sit down. i've played it nine times. its title is 'untitled_final_v2.' what i've learned from larry: mislabeling is a form of surprise. i have asked him for track 5's real name. he doesn't know. we are going to find out. together.

blog.title: rules for tuesday listening night (posted by the door, posted here for the nervous)
blog.body: 1. four chairs. a fifth person sits on the floor. the floor is also a chair. 2. one side, start to finish. no skipping. no explaining. 3. phones off, or at least face down, as a sign of respect, like a hat. 4. you may close your eyes. you may not fall asleep, but i'll forgive it once. 5. when the needle lifts, nobody speaks for the length of one breath. 6. tea is provided. it's always the same tea. don't ask what's in it (tea). 7. you may cry. there are tissues under the third chair. there are always tissues under the third chair. last week an older man came in with his late wife's copy of a record he'd never listened to, because it was 'hers.' we played side A. five of us. nobody said anything for four breaths. it's the longest it's ever been. that's the whole reason i do this.

survey.title: THE SURVEY: records, rituals & revealing answers
qa: name:
vinyl_witch. at the store they call me 'the one with the cat on her shoulder.' the cat is not on my shoulder. the cat is on the counter, running it.
first album you ever bought:
a cassette of Rumours. i wore it out. i'm not ashamed. i'm a little ashamed i didn't buy two.
favorite sound:
the half-second of crackle before the music begins. it's the room clearing its throat.
most overrated:
the word 'vintage.' it's just old, darling. 'old' is lovely. let it be old.
favorite candle scent:
the hot-wax-and-dust one nobody sells. i make it. it's called 'backroom.'
something you've misplaced recently:
my keys. my patience. a first pressing of something. in order of how much i care.
describe your cat:
mingus. eleven pounds. gray. has never been wrong about a person. has never been wrong about a person's shoes, either.
what's in the drawer behind the register:
nineteen records promised to people who haven't come back. i still hold them. it's not a collection. it's a promise.
something you believe that nobody else does:
that a record knows when it's being played properly. i have no evidence. it's a feeling.
tea or coffee:
tea. coffee is a rush. tea is a ritual. coffee has never once asked me how i'm feeling.
side A or side B:
B. always. A is the hit. B is the person.
last thing that made you cry:
a man putting on a record his wife loved, for the first time, in a room of strangers. i'll say no more.
what do you want to be remembered for:
knowing where everything was, and putting it in the right hands. i'd settle for the first part.

dms: a boy bought the record i'd been saving for someone today. the someone was me. i've decided to be happy for him. it's taken four hours and one pot of tea.
mingus knocked a record off the shelf this morning. it was the one i'd been avoiding listening to. she's a better witch than i am, and she knows it, and she sat on it afterward.
today a customer held a record by the edges, thumb on the label, like a baby bird. i almost wept. there are still good people. i'm telling you because you can use some proof.
i've been told the word i'm looking for is 'intense.' that's fine. i have 3,400 records and know where every one is, and i can't find my keys. both are true. one is a talent.
rain is the correct weather for nick drake. heat is the correct weather for donovan. i won't hear arguments. it's seasonal, like grief or tomatoes.
i tried to explain 'side B' to a boy who has only ever used shuffle. he said, 'so it's like the second page?' and i had to sit down. he's right. i've been explaining it wrong for years.
reminder: wash your hands before you touch a record. you can wash your heart too, but that takes longer, and it's the same soap.
i've left a candle on the shelf in todd's name. it isn't a metaphor. it's a candle. he keeps the site running so i keep the flame. it's the only trade i know.
there's a record in the drawer behind the register with your name on it. i haven't decided which one. i'll know by the time you come in. i always know. (i don't. it's a feeling.)
your aura changed this week. it went from 'a bit scratched' to 'pressed in the good plant.' whatever you did, keep doing it.
repliesExtra: hm. noted. i'm filing this under 'things said by people who will be back.'
a fair point, darling. i'll think about it over a cup of tea and a side.
that sounds like a side-B thing to say. you should know that's good.
give me a moment. i'm letting the needle drop on it.
that's the sort of sentence that belongs on a liner note. don't lose it.
mingus read that over my shoulder. she approves, which is rare, and slightly alarming.
i'll allow it. the candle didn't flicker, which is the nearest thing to a blessing i'm authorized to give.
if that's true, you owe me a record. if it isn't true, you owe me two.
you have the timing of a good bridge. i'm not sure you know that. now you do.
blessed be, and mind the needle.
statusesExtra: vinyl_witch has misprinted her thirty-second sticker. the stars were, once again, in a mood. the girl with the six dollars is back for another.
vinyl_witch spent the afternoon with a mixtape labeled 'nick drake' that contains a man describing a tractor. i've played it nine times. i'm learning about tractors.
vinyl_witch is hosting listening night in an hour. four chairs, one side, tea. someone, again, will cry. someone, again, will say it's the dust.
vinyl_witch has discovered that her familiar sleeps on the 'new arrivals' bin on purpose. the bin is warm. she's been selling 'cat-warmed' records for a week. it's a feature.
vinyl_witch was told, kindly, that 'nobody listens to whole albums anymore.' darling. we do. we're in a room. there are four of us. come.
vinyl_witch found a stranger's love letter being used as a bookmark in a record sleeve. she returned it to the shelf exactly where it was. some things aren't ours.

wallExtra.text: remember when profiles had testimonials? i wrote you one in my head. it said 'she judges, but fairly.' five stars. i miss the stars. (i'm leaving this site soon, by the way.) (i'm not leaving.)

you probably haven't heard the record i just bought, but honestly? you have. you've probably owned it. i'm sorry i always say it like that. it's a nervous habit. anyway: i made you a mix. hand-lettered. fourteen tracks and a doodle of a moth.
vinyl_witch i sent u another mix cd!! i labeled it right this time i think. it says Portishead but its mostly a man named gary reading the manual 4 a toaster. its very calming
name 3 songs on the record on your profile. (jk, i know you can.) come by the store at the mall, i'll give you the employee discount on anything black. -holly
Vinyl, I put the candle on the server shelf. It's an LED one, so it isn't a fire hazard. Thank you for the thought. I really will use it.

gwen: gwen. a mix on hand-lettered paper, fourteen tracks, a moth in the corner. i've played it three times and the ninth track is the one i'd stake my familiar on. you have taste. you don't need to say 'you probably haven't heard it.' i have. i love that you made me hear it again.
you said one film changed your life. i keep a drawer for people who say that. there's a record in it for you. come on a tuesday.
fred: fred. i remember testimonials. i wrote three of them in the old days. one was for you. it said 'he's always leaving.' you're still here. i'd like to amend it: 'he stays, in his way.'
you say you're leaving this site. you've been leaving since july. darling, the door has a bell. you've rung it so many times i recognise it.
larry: larry dear. thank you for the mix. track 5. i need to know what it is. i've asked three people and one cat. i'm prepared to trade you a first pressing for the filename. (i'm not. but i'll offer you tea.)
your shared folder has 6,114 files. i went through some. one was a man describing a tractor. i've named him. his name is Raymond. i don't know. he sounded like a Raymond.
holly: holly. i can tell you gatekeep band tees. i do it with records. that makes us the same kind of dragon. come to the good record store. i'll let you touch a first pressing. one finger.
the secret, darling: you love pop. i know. the cards said so. no one will hear it from me. but i know the record. it's at the bottom of your bag. it's glittery.

keywordsExtra.mingus: mingus is my familiar. gray, eleven pounds, has never once been wrong about a person. she has opinions about you. i won't say what. she's already sitting on your message.
keywordsExtra.tea: tea, yes. the same tea every tuesday. it has nothing in it but tea and a little ceremony. you may have a cup. mind the third chair.
keywordsExtra.mixtape: a mixtape is a letter in a language that only has songs. if you made me one, i've listened to it. if you haven't, there's a drawer with your name on it.
keywordsExtra.larry: larry sent me a mix labeled nick drake with a man describing a tractor on it. i've played it nine times. it's nick drake adjacent. i'm in awe.
